docs.text: From satellite observations to a fuel-moisture map lfmc-multisensor estimates live fuel moisture content (LFMC) from satellite reflectance, weather and terrain. LFMC is water mass as a percentage of dry vegetation mass: 100% means equal water and dry masses, and values above 100% are possible. The package applies the published vegetation models to a chosen area and date, then saves the predictions with quality codes and input provenance. It does not train a new model during a mapping run. Explore LFMC maps online The EOSIAL Fire Weather Viewer lets you explore published 8-day Suomi NPP VIIRS LFMC maps for the western United States in your browser. It requires no installation or provider accounts. Open the Fire Weather Viewer Browse and download maps. Switch between composites, adjust the colour palette and opacity, or download a GeoTIFF and view its provenance. Chart a point or area. Click a pixel to inspect its LFMC estimate and use Show LFMC chart to see its history. With Query area time series , drag and release a rectangle or select two opposite corners to chart the mean and interquartile range (the 25th–75th percentiles) of valid pixels for each composite. Find field sampling locations. Enable Globe-LFMC 2.0 sampling sites to see historical field locations and click a marker to identify the site. Generate your own maps Start with the small Sentinel-2 Camp Fire example before changing the area or product. This gives you a known configuration for checking installation, provider access and the model files. Use the desktop GUI if you prefer selecting a shapefile and filling in a form. The command-line tutorial walks through the same processing stages with an explicit JSON request. Historical Camp Fire example from Figure A3 of Pampanoni et al. (2026), reproduced unmodified under CC BY 4.0. See citation and attribution . Direct workflows use a selected WorldCover 2021 or 2020 snapshot. Install in Conda and supply the trusted model bundles. Configure your provider access . Make your first map . Read LFMC, QA and provenance . Change the configuration for another supported example. Summarise the AOI through time , overall and by vegetation type. The method and validation guide explains how inputs become predictions, including optional weather adjustment. Consult troubleshooting when a run stops or returns few valid pixels. The current candidate defaults to WorldCover 2021 for any acquisition year; 2020 is selectable. Enter a single date or an inclusive date range in the GUI. Range runs produce one map per matching scene and a manifest of completed maps. Downloads can be substantial even for a small area because some products require complete source assets. Keep the cache for subsequent runs. Accounts and model files belong on your machine; they are not supplied by a documentation website. Project updates and feedback Further research may lead to updates to the LFMC models. Planned work includes validated support for Sentinel-2C, Sentinel-3C and additional satellites. Feedback from researchers, fire managers and other users is welcome. Share feedback on GitHub

docs.text: Configure provider access Each user supplies their own credentials. Keep them in environment variables or the provider's external configuration file, outside this repository. Credentials do not belong in JSON configurations, notebooks, provenance records or commits. The first tutorial needs Copernicus Data Space access for Sentinel-2 and Climate Data Store access for daily weather. Other products use the routes below. Input Access needed Configuration read by the package Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-3 Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem (CDSE) account and S3 keys CDSE_S3_ACCESS_KEY , CDSE_S3_SECRET_KEY MODIS and VIIRS NASA Earthdata account with applicable data access External .netrc / _netrc , or EARTHDATA_TOKEN , or EARTHDATA_USERNAME and EARTHDATA_PASSWORD AgERA5 weather, all products Copernicus Climate Data Store (CDS) account and accepted dataset terms External .cdsapirc or supported CDS client environment settings Landsat 8/9 Public Planetary Computer archive No user credential in the exercised route WorldCover and AW3D30 v4.1 Public data services and applicable terms No additional credential in the exercised region. The JAXA archive fallback can use optional JAXA_USERNAME and JAXA_PASSWORD . Optional historical weather reference Pinned public NCAR/GDEX source No additional credential in the exercised route Copernicus Data Space Register or sign in to Copernicus Data Space and open the S3 credentials manager . Choose Add Credentials , set an expiry date and confirm. Save the access key and secret key securely. The secret is shown once. CDSE S3 instructions In a Windows PowerShell terminal with the LFMC Conda environment activated, copy and run each line exactly as shown. When the terminal asks for a key, paste only the key and press Enter. The quoted labels are the prompts you will see. Leave them as written. PowerShell masks the secret key as you enter it. $env:CDSE_S3_ACCESS_KEY = Read-Host "CDSE access key" $env:CDSE_S3_SECRET_KEY = [System.Net.NetworkCredential]::new('', (Read-Host "CDSE secret key" -AsSecureString)).Password If your terminal is Command Prompt (cmd.exe) , including Anaconda Prompt, use these commands instead. Run each line as written and paste the key when prompted. Command Prompt displays what you enter. set /p "CDSE_S3_ACCESS_KEY=CDSE access key: " set /p "CDSE_S3_SECRET_KEY=CDSE secret key: " Run the access check and launch the LFMC GUI or CLI from the same terminal so it can read the keys. These settings last until you close that terminal. Generate a new pair when the keys expire. Sentinel-2 uses S3 to read native AOI windows from reflectance and raster masks. Sentinel-3 also uses S3 and downloads the complete files it needs from the selected swath. Sentinel-2 also has an OAuth implementation using CDSE_ACCESS_TOKEN or CDSE_USERNAME / CDSE_PASSWORD ; its download route has not received the same live validation and downloads complete required SAFE files. Sentinel-3 currently requires the S3 keys. Prefer the exercised S3 route for the tutorial. Climate Data Store On the CDS API setup page , follow 1. Setup the CDS Api key . Register or sign in, then copy the two configuration lines beginning with url: and key: . The page shows a Unix path for the file. On Windows, use the location in the next step. Save those lines in %USERPROFILE%\.cdsapirc on Windows. In Notepad, choose All files when saving and make sure the name is exactly .cdsapirc . While signed in, open the AgERA5 dataset , select Download and accept the terms at the bottom of the form. Every satellite workflow needs CDS access. The Conda environment includes the CDS client. LFMC requests the daily weather and rainfall history for you. Provider request queues and processing affect download time. An account may be configured correctly while a request is still waiting for completion. NASA Earthdata Register or sign in at Earthdata Login . If the data service asks you to authorise access, approve the relevant LP DAAC application. NASA application authorisation From your profile, choose Generate Token and copy the token when displayed. NASA token instructions In PowerShell with the LFMC Conda environment activated, copy and run this line as written. Paste the token at the masked prompt and press Enter. $env:EARTHDATA_TOKEN = [System.Net.NetworkCredential]::new('', (Read-Host "Earthdata token" -AsSecureString)).Password If you are using Command Prompt (cmd.exe) , run this line as written and paste the token when prompted. Command Prompt displays what you enter. set /p "EARTHDATA_TOKEN=Earthdata token: " Launch LFMC from the same terminal. You can also use a home-directory .netrc or _netrc with an urs.earthdata.nasa.gov entry, or set both EARTHDATA_USERNAME and EARTHDATA_PASSWORD . NASA netrc instructions Check what the package can find In your activated Conda environment: lfmc-multisensor access-check examples/sentinel2_camp_fire_2018.json The command reports whether configuration is present, without returning secret values. It does not authenticate against each provider or prove that terms have been accepted. Public catalogue discovery can succeed even when an authenticated download will fail. A download failure should be checked against the account, keys or terms required for that particular input. Next, make the first map .

docs.text: Choose the area, date and satellite A JSON configuration makes the inference choices explicit and keeps credentials separate from the request. Begin with the example for your satellite. Paths are resolved relative to that JSON file. Use relative paths or explicit absolute paths; ~ is not expanded. In Windows JSON paths, use forward slashes or escape each backslash as \\ . Shared settings Setting Meaning aoi_path Polygon shapefile, or WGS84 GeoJSON; the primary file-based AOI option aoi_circle Alternative point/radius object with latitude , longitude and radius_km aoi_square Alternative point/square object with latitude , longitude and full side_km bounds Alternative [west, south, east, north] in WGS84 longitude/latitude degrees day YYYY-MM-DD ; single/start date, beginning at 00:00 UTC end_day Optional inclusive end date; omit or leave empty for a single day max_cloud_cover Optional inclusive maximum catalogue cloud percentage, 0–100; null (default) means no limit include_unknown_cloud With a maximum set, retain scenes whose percentage is unavailable; defaults to false product Optical product identifier; omitted only for the default s2_l2a sensor Explicit spacecraft/domain where required; see below landcover_year Defaults to 2021; 2020 is also available, independently of acquisition year landcover_policy Defaults to fixed-year ; older same-year-annual requests are migrated to this policy models_dir Directory holding the three trusted published bundles cache_dir Directory for reusable source inputs and prepared files output Directory, default filename label, and extension ( .tif for affine grids or .nc for Sentinel-3) output_label Optional editable filename prefix; defaults to the polygon file's stem, otherwise the output's existing stem statistics Generate AOI statistics and figures after mapping; defaults to false statistics_by_vegetation Also summarise Grass, Shrub and Tree; defaults to true statistics_centre Figure line: median (default) or mean ; the CSV contains both statistics_support available (default) or common valid native pixels statistics_comparisons Optional exploratory paired-date intervals; defaults to false ; requires common support and vegetation groups statistics_block_length Temporal block length in dates; default 3 statistics_source Saved series manifest or LFMC output to analyse with the statistics command downscale Optional weather adjustment; defaults to false product_ids One selected scene for a single day; optional subset of scenes in range mode, otherwise all matches The initial adapters accept non-crossing areas no more than one degree across, within 60 degrees south to 60 degrees north. Each map handles one scene or granule; a time series processes the matching scenes sequentially as separate maps. For affine products, an AOI crossing the selected source grid is rejected. Sentinel-3 records the native centres inside the requested area; the selected scene may cover only part of it. There is no automatic multi-scene mosaic. Set one of aoi_path , aoi_circle , aoi_square or bounds . Shapefile components must share a base name and include .shp , .shx , .dbf and .prj . All polygon features are unioned, reprojected from the declared CRS and applied as a pixel-centre mask. Holes remain excluded. Download bounds are derived automatically; they do not replace the polygon mask. File and geometry hashes distinguish AOIs with different boundaries even when they share the same bounding rectangle. "aoi_path": "aoi/sardinia.shp" See examples/sentinel2_shapefile_2021.json and the desktop GUI guide. For a circular AOI without an input polygon file, use: "aoi_circle": {"latitude": 40.01, "longitude": 8.76, "radius_km": 0.75} This constructs a WGS84 geodesic circle polygon with 720 boundary vertices. Its derived bounds limit acquisition and its polygon masks native pixel centres. The point, radius, construction method and geometry hash are retained in provenance. The full circle must satisfy the same geographic/area limits; it does not enable crossing the antimeridian or mosaicking scenes. See examples/sentinel2_point_radius_2021.json . For a centred square, use: "aoi_square": {"latitude": 40.01, "longitude": 8.76, "side_km": 1.5} This defines the full side length in kilometres, aligned east/north in a local azimuthal equidistant projection. Densified edges are transformed to WGS84. See examples/sentinel2_square_2021.json . For polygon-file AOIs, the default output label comes from the filename stem. An aoi_path ending in Forest reserve.shp and output: "maps/test.tif" produce maps/Forest reserve_<source-product>_LFMC_v01.tif . Set output_label: "My study" to change the prefix. Use a non-empty portable filename component without path separators or reserved characters. The GUI shows the output prefix while the form is edited. Scene discovery supplies the source product identifier. Per-map provenance lists the actual filenames. WorldCover 2021 is the default for all acquisition years, including 2023. Set landcover_year: 2020 to use the alternative snapshot. The selected map stays fixed throughout a time series; it may not represent land-cover changes after its reference year. No other land-cover maps are implemented yet. Single days and inclusive date ranges With only day , discovery searches that complete UTC day. With end_day , it searches from 00:00 of day through all of the final minute of end_day , including seconds and fractional seconds. Where the catalogue supports it, the implementation uses midnight of the following day as an exclusive upper bound. End dates before the start date are rejected. "day": "2023-07-01", "end_day": "2023-07-31", "landcover_year": 2021 Range-mode run processes all matching scenes, or the subset in product_ids . Sentinel-2, Landsat and Sentinel-3 use each scene's acquisition date for weather and calendar features. Multiple scenes on the same date remain separate maps; no gap filling, nearby-date substitution or mosaicking is applied. See examples/sentinel2_timeseries_2023.json . Product-specific settings Product product sensor tile Extra choice Sentinel-2 L2A s2_l2a Read from selected SAFE Optional MGRS, e.g. 32TMK , without leading T Exact UTC acquisition date Landsat 8 / 9 landsat_c2l2 L8/L9 for both, L8 or L9 for one Optional six-digit WRS path/row, e.g. 193032 Exact UTC acquisition date MODIS Terra/Aqua modis Terra/Aqua MODIS for both, Terra MODIS for Terra Optional sinusoidal tile, e.g. h18v04 Explicit composite policy Suomi NPP VIIRS viirs Suomi NPP VIIRS Same optional convention Explicit composite policy Sentinel-3 s3syn300 S3A/S3B for both, S3A or S3B for one Empty NTC collection 002, .nc output Only calibrated spacecraft domains are accepted. NOAA VIIRS spacecraft and other products are not substituted for the published Suomi NPP domain. Existing Aqua-only configurations use modis_aqua with Aqua MODIS . The grouped MODIS setting preserves the Terra or Aqua calibration and source granule ID in each map. Eight-day composites MODIS and VIIRS require: "composite_policy": "contains-analysis-date" The selected interval is anchored at day 1 of the year and contains day . For example, 22 July 2021 selects 20 through 27 July, with an exclusive end of 28 July. Weather and day-of-year predictors use the configured analysis date. Reflectance may originate from another day within the composite, including a later day. This is a retrospective retrieval and depends on completed processing. The adapter does not replace the configured weather date with a per-pixel observation date. A MODIS/VIIRS range finds the eight-day composites overlapping the requested days, including the composite containing the start date. It processes each matching granule once. The first composite uses the requested start date as its weather/analysis date; later composites use their start dates. This also applies across calendar years. The final composite can contain observations after the requested end date, so the explicit composite confirmation remains required. Scene selection and repeated runs discover returns the current catalogue candidates. For a single date with several matches, insert one returned ID in product_ids . In range mode, omit IDs to process all matching scenes, or provide several IDs to choose a subset. The workflow does not choose the first candidate, search a nearby date or switch spacecraft when a scene is missing. For output: "maps/lfmc.tif" , a range writes names such as lfmc_<source-product>_LFMC_v01.tif , normal QA/provenance companions and lfmc_timeseries.json . Sentinel-3 uses .nc for each native map. The manifest records the requested interval, fixed WorldCover year and completed maps. It updates after each map and records a failure without discarding earlier results. An interrupted worker can leave its manifest marked running ; completed maps remain valid. To retry, choose a new output prefix and reuse the cache, or request only the unfinished scene IDs with a new prefix. Existing final outputs and manifests are protected from replacement. Choose another output filename for a repeated run or a different weather mode. Keep the same cache when inputs can be reused. A cached request does not remove the need for valid provider configuration or guarantee that the complete run will work offline.

docs.text: MODIS and VIIRS require: "composite_policy": "contains-analysis-date" The selected interval is anchored at day 1 of the year and contains day . docs.text: discover returns the current catalogue candidates. For a single date with several matches, insert one returned ID in product_ids . docs.text: Use the desktop interface The desktop GUI provides file pickers and a form for the same inference workflow used by the command line. Shapefile selection is the default way to define the area of interest. You can also enter a longitude/latitude bounding box or define a circle or square around a point. Processing runs locally in your Conda environment. The documentation website does not run models or collect provider credentials. Start the application Complete installation, configure provider access and obtain the trusted model bundles first. In an activated Conda terminal, run: lfmc-multisensor gui Alternatively, use lfmc-multisensor-gui or python -m lfmc_multisensor.gui . Use the current installed package so that it includes the GUI and polygon dependencies. Tkinter/Tcl/Tk supplies the desktop widgets; the provided Conda installation includes Tk. Other installations may need the matching Conda tk package. Select the folder containing the three model files and click Check models before starting a download. 1. Choose the area Select Shapefile / polygon file and browse to a .shp file. Keep its .shx , .dbf and .prj components beside it with the same base name. The .prj must declare the coordinate reference system. The loader does not guess a missing CRS. WGS84 GeoJSON polygons are also accepted. All polygon features are combined into one area. Interior holes and disconnected parts are retained. A projected shapefile is reprojected to WGS84 for discovery and masking. Invalid, empty or non-polygon features stop validation with a message; they are not silently dropped or repaired. The bounding rectangle limits acquisition and determines the native raster window. A prediction is retained only when its pixel centre lies on or inside the polygon union; hole interiors are excluded. The saved grid remains native, with no-data outside the selected polygons. Input footprints are not reshaped or resampled to make polygon boundaries look smoother. For the first map, use Load configuration to open examples/sentinel2_camp_fire_2018.json . It selects a Sentinel-2 scene and a small bounding box in the Camp Fire study area. To try shapefile masking, load examples/sentinel2_shapefile_2021.json using Load configuration . Its manually drawn Sardinia AOI includes a cut corner and a small hole to demonstrate masking. It is not a field-site or fire-perimeter dataset. Replace the models/cache/output paths for your installation. For a simple rectangle, choose Bounding box (WGS84) and enter west, south, east and north. Coordinates are longitude/latitude degrees. Original bounding-box configurations continue to work. To create an AOI on the fly, choose Point and radius . Enter latitude and longitude in WGS84 decimal degrees, then Radius (km) . For example, latitude 40.01 , longitude 8.76 and radius 0.75 define a circle extending 750 metres from the point. The value is a radius, not a diameter. The application constructs a polygon from 720 boundary points at that distance on the WGS84 ellipsoid; it does not buffer longitude/latitude degrees as if they were metres. Pixel centres inside this polygon are retained on the satellite's native grid. The point and radius are stored directly in saved configurations, so no extra shapefile or GeoJSON is needed. Reloading restores this selection. Zero, negative or non-finite radii are rejected, as are circles crossing the antimeridian or exceeding the existing geographic and one-degree area limits. Reduce the radius if the plan reports an unsupported extent. A very small circle may contain no pixel centres on a coarse satellite grid. For a square, choose Point and square and enter its centre latitude, longitude and Side (km) . A side of 1.5 creates a 1.5 by 1.5 km area; this value is the full side length, not a radius or half-width. The square is aligned east/north in a local metric projection centred on the point. Its boundary is transformed to WGS84 for discovery and native pixel-centre masking. The same geographic and area limits apply to the whole square. Both circle and square settings are preserved when saving and loading a configuration. 2. Select a satellite, dates and WorldCover map Max cloud (%) optionally limits discovery to scenes at or below a percentage between 0 and 100. Leave it blank for an unrestricted search. Include unknown cloud cover retains scenes without a usable catalogue percentage when a maximum is set; otherwise those scenes are excluded. Without a maximum, all scenes remain eligible, including those with missing percentages. The scene selection window shows a Cloud (%) column, with N/A for missing values. Click its heading to sort, or use Apply list filter to narrow the returned scenes before selecting them. Percentages are displayed to two decimal places; filtering uses the original precision and includes the maximum itself. The chosen list filter is saved in the main form and applied again during Run. Changing the main cloud settings clears previous scene selections. To recover scenes excluded by the original search, widen its limit and search again. Cloud percentages describe the provider's whole scene or granule, rather than the selected AOI. They do not replace pixel quality masks. Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-3 use the CDSE cloudCover attribute when available; Landsat uses STAC eo:cloud_cover ; MODIS/VIIRS use CMR cloud_cover . Some products, especially composites, have no usable percentage and will show N/A. Missing, invalid or ambiguous metadata is never interpreted as zero cloud. These metadata definitions are documented by CDSE , STAC EO and NASA CMR . Choose the product from the menu. Landsat 8 / 9 searches both spacecraft. Each selected Landsat scene uses its spacecraft's calibration. If a saved configuration specifies just one Landsat spacecraft, the form displays that restriction. Select Landsat 8 / 9 again to search both. Sentinel-3 SYNERGY works the same way for Sentinel-3A and Sentinel-3B. MODIS (Terra/Aqua) searches both spacecraft. Scene IDs start with MOD09A1 for Terra and MYD09A1 for Aqua. A saved spacecraft-specific configuration keeps its original search scope. Select MODIS (Terra/Aqua) again to search both. Enter the actual acquisition date for Sentinel-2, Landsat or Sentinel-3. For MODIS/VIIRS, enter the analysis date and explicitly confirm use of the containing eight-day composite. Such a composite can include observations after the analysis date. Enter the date in Single / start date (UTC) . Leave End date (optional) blank to search from 00:00 through 23:59 of that one day, including its final seconds. Set an end date to search the complete inclusive interval. A range run writes one native map per matching scene using each acquisition's own weather date. End dates before the start date are rejected. Setting the same start and end date enables a range run over all matching scenes on that day. The WorldCover map defaults to 2021 , even for a request in 2023 or another acquisition year. Select 2020 for the alternative snapshot. The chosen map stays fixed across the time series; additional maps are future work. For MODIS/VIIRS ranges, each overlapping eight-day granule is processed once. The first composite uses the requested start date for weather; later composites use their start dates. A final composite can include observations after the end date. Keep the explicit composite confirmation selected when using these products. The tile/WRS filter is optional. It can narrow discovery when you know the desired grid, but you can search from the area and date without supplying one. Sentinel-3 uses no tile filter. Each output remains a single scene/granule, with areas no more than one degree across within 60 degrees south to 60 degrees north. Polygon or date-range selection does not enable mosaicking. Actual optical and weather availability still determine which dates can be processed. 3. Select models, cache and output Choose the directory containing the three authorised model bundles, a cache directory and a new output path. Most products write .tif ; Sentinel-3 writes .nc with two-dimensional coordinates. Switching products updates the expected extension. Existing final outputs are protected from replacement. Filename label sets the prefix before the source product ID and the _LFMC_v01 suffix. Selecting Forest reserve.shp defaults the label to Forest reserve . The output selection sets the directory and extension. The label follows changes to the selected file until you edit it. Your custom label then stays in place; Use AOI name restores the automatic default. Choosing or editing an output filename also updates the label. Saved configurations preserve the chosen label. There is no required test prefix. For a time series, choosing lfmc.tif also writes lfmc_timeseries.json . The manifest updates as each scene completes; it links the individual maps and their provenance. Generated maps record the model-set version and the individual grass, shrub and tree model versions. The current published weights are registered as 1.0.0 ; this labels the existing weights and does not retrain them. See the output metadata guide for the tags and provenance fields. Leave the optional weather adjustment unchecked for the default weather mode. Selecting it applies the appendix methodology using the labelled historical reference approximation. It does not change the satellite grid or establish an improvement in field accuracy. 4. Inspect, discover and run Plan validates the form and explains the inputs without contacting providers. For a polygon, its CRS, bounds, feature count and file fingerprints identify the selected AOI. Check access reports the presence of external provider configuration. It does not prove that credentials or dataset terms are valid. Check models verifies bundle hashes and compatibility before a download. Find scenes queries the requested area/date. One matching scene is selected automatically. For a single date, choose one if several match. For a range, choose multiple scenes or use Select all . Leaving scene IDs empty in range mode processes all matches. No ranking or mosaic is applied. Run checks the models, downloads/prepares inputs and predicts. Progress messages and errors appear in the log while the form stays responsive. Sentinel-2 over CDSE S3 reports the MB transferred for native AOI windows. Its activity bar animates while files are read because the compressed bytes needed by each window are only known as the reads complete. For Sentinel-3 over CDSE S3, the progress bar and status show the current file and the MB transferred across the files still needed for that scene. Verified cached files are reused. The bar returns to its activity animation when processing continues after the download. Sentinel-3 downloads the required geolocation, reflectance, QA, and manifest files for the selected swath. Cropping to the AOI happens locally after acquisition, so the first download can be sizeable even for a small circle. Changing either date clears old scene selections. If you change the area or satellite, find scenes again. A stale explicit scene ID is rejected if it does not belong to the new catalogue request. Save configuration writes a reusable JSON request without credentials. Load configuration restores the form, including polygon, point/radius or bounding-box mode. The run's request and log are stored under the selected cache's gui_requests directory. Outputs retain the normal QA and provenance companions. Cancel and recover Cancel stops the local worker. Keep the same cache folder when retrying a cancelled, interrupted or failed run. The next run reuses verified inputs and restarts any incomplete download from the beginning of that asset. One scene. Correct the error and click Run again. Use a new output label if the earlier attempt created any output files. Date range. Open the previous *_timeseries.json in a text editor. Its maps list contains the completed scene IDs and outputs, even if the status still says running after a hard stop. Use Find scenes and select the remaining scenes, leave the cache folder unchanged, and choose a new output label. This starts a second series and preserves the first series. Running the original full selection again would also predict the completed scenes. Only statistics failed. Open Statistics options / saved maps… and use Analyse saved outputs with a fresh statistics label. Some corrupt weather-cache entries require the manual check in troubleshooting . The GUI starts one task at a time and limits its worker's CPU/thread settings. Provider requests can still wait in a remote queue. A native-library failure in the worker is reported as a failed exit; it does not run inference inside the GUI event loop. The Pampanoni et al. (2026) link at the bottom right opens the paper's DOI page in your default web browser. It also works with keyboard focus and Enter. The footer remains visible while the form can scroll on smaller windows. AOI summaries and figures Select Calculate AOI statistics and figures after mapping for automatic summaries. Statistics options / saved maps… lets you choose median or mean, vegetation groups and available/common pixel support. It also provides Analyse saved outputs , which reads a completed series or map using the current AOI and filename label. This analysis needs no provider access or model loading. See the statistics tutorial for figures, coverage, older-map compatibility and optional exploratory vegetation contrasts.

docs.text: Install and check the environment Use Conda to provide Python and the geospatial libraries together. On Windows, activating the environment also sets the paths needed by GDAL and other native libraries. Calling an environment's python.exe directly does not provide the same setup. Clone the repository Install Git . In the parent folder where you want to keep the project, run: git clone https://github.com/valpamp/lfmc-multisensor.git cd lfmc-multisensor The public clone includes the three compressed model bundles in model-assets/ , about 170 MiB in total. Standard Git is sufficient. Tested Windows installation Install Miniforge for Windows x86_64 if Conda is unfamiliar or absent. An existing Conda installation also works. Open Miniforge Prompt from the Windows Start menu, or open the prompt for your existing Conda installation. Change to the cloned folder. For example, in that prompt run cd /d "C:\path\to\lfmc-multisensor" . Run these commands in that prompt. conda create -n lfmc-multisensor --file environment-win64.lock.txt conda activate lfmc-multisensor python -m pip install --require-hashes --no-deps -r requirements-statistics-win64.lock.txt python -m pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation . python -m pip check The explicit Conda file fixes the tested Windows package builds. The supplemental pip file supplies the HDF4 reader used by Terra/Aqua MODIS and the polygon AOI readers used by the GUI and shapefile configurations, plus Matplotlib and its plotting dependencies for AOI statistics. The statistics lock includes the workflow lock; CLI installations without figures can use requirements-workflow-win64.lock.txt instead. Installing this repository adds the lfmc-multisensor command. The lock includes build tools, so the installation can use them without creating a separate build environment. Check which environment is running: python -c "import sys, numpy, rasterio; print(sys.prefix); print(numpy.__version__); print(rasterio.__version__)" python -m lfmc_multisensor.cli plan examples/sentinel2_camp_fire_2018.json The printed prefix should identify the environment you just activated. The plan command does not download data. If a terminal cannot retain activation, use Conda to launch each command: conda run --no-capture-output -n lfmc-multisensor python -m lfmc_multisensor.cli plan examples/sentinel2_camp_fire_2018.json Supply the published models The checkout includes all three LFMC model bundles from model set 1.0.0 : model-assets/ best_Grass_gapfill_within_site.joblib.bz2 best_Shrub_gapfill_within_site.joblib.bz2 best_Tree_gapfill_within_site.joblib.bz2 The example configurations already refer to this directory. To use another location, change models_dir in the configuration. Paths are resolved relative to the configuration file, including when you run the CLI from another directory. In the GUI, select model-assets and click Check models before running the first map. Both Check models and a CLI run automatically extract and verify each bundle on first use. Allow about 600 MiB of extra space in the model directory for the extracted .joblib files. Subsequent runs reuse these files and verify them against the published SHA-256 checksums. The Windows environment above includes the required scikit-learn 1.9.0 . Only load files from a trusted source. Joblib/Python model serialisation can execute code; a model file is not an inert data table. docs.text: What the workflow estimates and what has been tested The package applies the models from the published multisensor LFMC study . For each eligible satellite location, it prepares reflectance, weather, terrain and seasonal predictors. Annual land cover selects the grass, shrub or tree model. The package puts the predictors in the order expected by that trained Random Forest, applies its stored scaling, and converts the model output back to LFMC as percent dry mass. Reflectance and vegetation models Product-specific screening removes missing or unsuitable optical observations. Reflectance is kept at the product's native support. Sentinel-2 uses B8A and B11 at 20 m and averages red B4 from 10 m. MODIS and VIIRS keep their actual sinusoidal spacing. Sentinel-3 retains its per-pixel geolocation. Before calculating spectral indices, each vegetation model applies its own stored calibration for the selected non-reference sensor and spacecraft. Sentinel-2 is the reference product and follows its reference preprocessing. The package does not fit new calibration coefficients or train a new forest during inference. Missing calibration domains stop the run. The indices, seasonal terms, ordered predictors, scaler and inverse target transformation follow the stored published bundles. Predictions require all of a model's inputs to be finite. LFMC outputs are not clipped to an arbitrary percentage range. Weather and optional elevation adjustment AgERA5 version 2 supplies daily weather on its native 0.1-degree grid. Its daily labels follow the provider's local-day convention. The package associates those labels with the configured analysis date, preserving the study's date convention; it does not reconstruct hourly weather at satellite overpass time. See the provider description . Predictors include daily conditions and rainfall totals over the preceding 3, 7, 28 and 84 days. Those antecedent totals exclude the analysis day; the daily rainfall predictor uses that day itself. Missing required history is not replaced by zero. By default, weather is interpolated to the satellite centres without the appendix elevation adjustment. Setting downscale: true applies the appendix constant-relative-humidity lapse methodology using local AW3D30 elevation and a reconstructed reference for the weather grid. That reference comes from a fixed historical field of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts' high-resolution (HRES) model. The reference is explicitly approximate: equivalence to the weather provider's exact terrain and requested date/cycle has not been verified. Both modes retain separate provenance. Terrain derivatives are calculated on the AW3D30 source grid before sampling. The optional adjustment changes weather predictors; it does not increase the resolution of the optical observation or establish a measured accuracy gain. Land cover and quality screening Direct workflows use WorldCover 2021 by default, with 2020 selectable. The map year is independent of the acquisition year and remains fixed across a time series. Changes in land cover after that snapshot are not reconstructed. The dominant category is selected among all map classes; only tree, shrub and grass categories route to a model. Training-site neighbourhood and suitability filters are not imposed on arbitrary inference locations. Sentinel-3 aggregates class fractions over nominal 300 m central rectangles in local UTM coordinates. Its audited metadata-based QA excludes cloud, snow and specified retrieval failures. This screening is stricter than the older appendix example's mask. The historical replay preserves its original mask; it is not a claim that the current direct QA reproduces every historical pixel. Historical Dynamic World probabilities are not acquired by these direct workflows. Evidence available for this candidate Three checks answer different questions: Saved-case replay: can extracted inference reproduce the saved appendix outputs and masks for the checked Sentinel-2 and native Sentinel-3 cases? Real-input reference comparison: do newly prepared inputs produce the same predictors and predictions through the package and the trusted research helpers? Installed-package exercise: does a built, non-editable package work outside the research source tree, with the recorded environment and provider access? The exercised Sardinia examples include all eight sensor/spacecraft paths in both weather modes. Their original and adjusted runs produced these valid-pixel counts: Example Acquisition or analysis date Valid pixels in each mode Sentinel-2 2021-07-22 8,701 Landsat 8 2021-07-15 3,047 Landsat 9 2021-11-18 3,047 Terra MODIS 2021-07-22, composite 20-27 July 16 Aqua MODIS 2021-07-22, same composite 6 Suomi NPP VIIRS 2021-07-22, same composite 16 Sentinel-3A 2021-07-22 42 Sentinel-3B 2021-07-21 49 The combined Windows check matched the baseline LFMC values and valid masks for all eight paths in both weather modes. Each original-mode path started with an empty provider cache. The downscaled paths reused the same checksum-verified historical weather reference. Later checks used cached inputs to verify polygon masking, the GUI and date-range processing. Reproducing software outputs is distinct from validating LFMC against independent field measurements. The small examples do not establish general geographic/date coverage, every processing baseline or operational real-time availability. Linux/macOS, additional land-cover maps, mosaics, and scientific accuracy of the optional weather adjustment remain outside the demonstrated scope.

docs.text: Read the map, quality codes and provenance LFMC is the mass of water in living vegetation expressed as a percentage of dry mass. Values can exceed 100%. These outputs are model estimates; they do not provide a separate uncertainty interval for each pixel. Always inspect the quality information alongside LFMC. No-data means that the workflow did not produce an eligible, complete prediction at that location. It must not be interpreted as zero moisture. The JSON request also records the optional cloud filter. Product provenance retains the provider-reported cloud_cover percentage and cloud_cover_source ; a missing percentage is JSON null . These values describe the catalogue scene/granule, rather than cloud coverage or valid-pixel coverage within the AOI. New LFMC maps carry copyright, licence and usage restrictions as GeoTIFF tags or global NetCDF attributes. See the repository's OUTPUT_TERMS.md for terms on sharing maps and obtaining a commercial licence. GeoTIFF products Sentinel-2, Landsat, MODIS and VIIRS write an LFMC raster, a QA raster, a dominant vegetation-class raster and a JSON record. For an output named map.tif , the companions are map_qa.tif , map_vegetation.tif and map.json . Keep all four together for statistics without the original input cache. The LFMC band is float32 with missing values stored as no-data. Its CRS and transform describe the native output grid. QA value Meaning How to use it 0 Valid LFMC estimate Include in analyses of predictions 1 Land cover does not route to a grass, shrub or tree model, or routing support is invalid Treat as unpredicted 2 Optical input is missing or rejected by product quality screening at a routed location Treat as unpredicted 3 A routed location has incomplete required predictors Inspect weather and terrain support 4 Pixel centre is outside the selected polygon AOI Treat as unpredicted; the rectangular native grid is retained 255 Raster no-data marker Treat as unpredicted Each pixel has one reported reason. For example, non-routed land cover is recorded even when optical inputs are also missing. QA is not a confidence score or a probability that a valid prediction is accurate. Sentinel-3 NetCDF Sentinel-3 pixels lie on a curved two-dimensional geolocation grid. The .nc output keeps that geometry rather than assigning a constant affine transform. The companion .json file records provenance. Variable Contents LFMC Moisture estimate, float32, percent dry mass QA Quality reason; codes 0-3 as above, plus 4 outside the requested bounding box or polygon AOI lat , lon Two-dimensional decoded source coordinates source_row , source_column Indices in the original source scene dominant_class Dominant WorldCover code over the nominal central support landcover_support_fraction Fraction of that support represented by valid land-cover inputs The native rectangular subset includes a two-cell halo. Halo centres outside the requested bounds have QA code 4 and no LFMC prediction. The recorded support fraction is diagnostic; no new training-suitability threshold is applied to it. import xarray as xr with xr.open_dataset("outputs/sentinel3a_2021.nc") as data: valid_lfmc = data["LFMC"].where(data["QA"] == 0) print(valid_lfmc.count().item()) print(data["lat"].shape, data["lon"].shape) Use the latitude/longitude arrays when displaying or comparing native S3 data. A regular-grid GeoTIFF export would require an explicit resampling choice and is not implemented in this candidate. Model versions and filename labels Every newly generated LFMC GeoTIFF and its QA companion store LFMC_MODEL_SET_VERSION , LFMC_MODEL_VERSION_GRASS , LFMC_MODEL_VERSION_SHRUB and LFMC_MODEL_VERSION_TREE as metadata tags. The corresponding model SHA256 tags bind those versions to exact artefact bytes. Native Sentinel-3 NetCDF stores the same fields as global attributes. LFMC_OUTPUT_LABEL records the selected filename label. Maps use <label>_<source-product>_LFMC_v01.<extension> . The original Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-3 names retain their acquisition timestamps and baseline tokens. Landsat uses the full USGS Level-2 identifier, including its processing date when available from the source asset. MODIS and VIIRS preserve the native granule identifier and append Ayyyymmdd for the analysis date, which can differ from the start of the composite. QA, vegetation, and provenance companions use the same map stem. GeoTIFF tags and NetCDF global attributes include LFMC_MODEL_MAP_VERSION , LFMC_PAPER_DOI , LFMC_PAPER_URL , and LFMC_SOURCE_PRODUCT_NAME for maps created from a provider scene. Additional source tags record its catalogue identifier and its native baseline or collection when identifiable. The JSON provenance and time-series manifest include model_provenance , with the model-set identity/version and each vegetation model's version and SHA256. Existing model_sha256 records are retained in per-map provenance. The current set and all three models are 1.0.0 , assigned to the already published weights without changing their contents. These versions are independent of the package version. Existing old outputs are not modified retroactively. import rasterio with rasterio.open("outputs/Forest reserve_<source-product>_LFMC_v01.tif") as data: print(data.tags()["LFMC_MODEL_SET_VERSION"]) print(data.tags()["LFMC_MODEL_VERSION_TREE"]) The loader verifies each bundle's checksum against the published model manifest before loading it. Time-series outputs Setting an end date writes separate native maps for matching scenes. The additional <prefix>_timeseries.json manifest lists completed maps, dates, selected inputs and status. It is updated after each map, so earlier completed results remain available if a later scene fails. These files are a collection of native maps, rather than a regridded temporal cube. Scene footprints, grids and valid pixels can differ. There is no temporal interpolation, compositing across separate scenes or automatic gap filling. WorldCover remains at the selected fixed reference year throughout the series. The optional AOI statistics add tables and mean/median figures, overall or by vegetation class. They can also be generated from saved outputs without repeating inference. Spatial spread bands are distinct from the optional exploratory intervals for paired-date vegetation contrasts. Provenance and comparisons The JSON record identifies the optical source, date or composite interval, land-cover policy, weather mode, model identities and checksums of inputs and outputs. Preserve it when sharing a map. It allows another run to distinguish a changed source scene, model or processing choice from a numerical discrepancy. Output pixel spacing describes the satellite grid. Weather starts from the native AgERA5 grid, and terrain starts from AW3D30. Interpolation and optional weather adjustment do not turn those inputs into independent measurements at every satellite pixel. Comparisons between sensors must also account for their different footprints, dates, composite intervals and masks.

docs.text: Summarise LFMC through time AOI statistics turn a collection of LFMC maps into a table and time-series figures. You can summarise the whole selected area and separately examine Grass, Shrub and Tree, using the same dominant vegetation categories that selected the inference models. The analysis reads saved predictions and QA; it does not download data or load the model bundles again. Synthetic demonstration of the figure format, not field observations. The lower panel reports the fraction of each group retained on common support. Use the desktop interface Before a new mapping run, select Calculate AOI statistics and figures after mapping . Open Statistics options / saved maps… to choose: Summary line: median, with a shaded spatial interquartile range; or mean, with a shaded band of one spatial standard deviation. Vegetation groups: retain the overall AOI summary and add Grass, Shrub and Tree. An absent or entirely invalid class remains missing, rather than receiving an LFMC value of zero. Pixel support: available valid pixels on each date, or common valid pixels across every map. The coverage panel and CSV counts show how much support contributes to the summaries. For an existing run, use the same options window to select its <label>_timeseries.json , a single LFMC GeoTIFF/NetCDF, or a per-map provenance JSON. Choose the AOI in the main form, set a filename label for the analysis, then click Analyse saved outputs . All completed maps in that source are analysed; the main date fields govern new mapping, rather than filtering this saved source. Models and provider credentials are not needed for this action. Statistics use the current polygon, circle, square or bounding box to select native pixel centres. The original map's valid footprint still limits coverage; selecting a larger AOI does not create observations outside it. Multiple features in a polygon file are treated as their union, as in mapping. Available or common support Available summarises the valid pixels independently on each date. It works with shifted native grids, including different Sentinel-3 overpasses. Cloud screening and changing coverage can alter which parts of a class contribute, so read the coverage panel alongside the LFMC curves. Common retains only pixel centres with valid predictions in every map. This is closest to the fixed-support summaries used in the paper's case studies. The maps must have identical grids and coordinates, and vegetation routing must agree on those common pixels. Shifted grids are rejected; no resampling is performed. A long or cloudy series can leave very few common pixels, or none. The table reports both available and retained counts. Summaries give equal weight to native pixel centres. They are not area-weighted statistics or fractions of pure vegetation cover. Grouping follows the maps' recorded model-routing categories and land-cover snapshot, rather than applying the GUI's land-cover selector to the saved maps again. Mixed products, weather modes, land-cover snapshots or model identities are rejected in one analysis. Compare vegetation types With vegetation groups enabled, the analysis also writes paired-date differences for Grass minus Shrub, Grass minus Tree and Shrub minus Tree. These differences are in LFMC percentage points . For example, class medians of 90% and 120% give a difference of −30 percentage points. Their temporal plot helps identify persistent contrasts and dates when those contrasts change. The shaded bands on the main figure describe spatial variability , not prediction confidence or statistical significance. Thousands of neighbouring pixels are not treated as independent replicates. For an optional exploratory temporal assessment, select Estimate exploratory paired-date vegetation contrast intervals . This selects common support and vegetation grouping. The calculation resamples blocks of consecutive paired dates, using a circular block bootstrap, and estimates an interval for the mean or median across those paired-date differences. The three intervals use a Bonferroni adjustment for a familywise confidence level of 95%. The method and end-to-start block construction are described in the bootstrap toolkit documentation . The package implements the small NumPy resampling calculation directly; that external toolkit is not a dependency. Intervals require unique, regularly spaced paired dates, common support and at least max(12, 4 × block length) paired observations. The default block length is three dates, with 2,000 resamples and recorded random seeds. These minimums are operational safeguards, not a guarantee of reliable inference. The method assumes that the paired-difference process is sufficiently stable over the selected period; that assumption is not automatically established. Seasonal trends, disturbances and long dependence can make it unsuitable. The comparison CSV reports interval limits and whether they exclude zero. This is exploratory evidence about model-derived temporal contrasts on the selected common pixels , conditional on the assumptions. It does not establish a causal vegetation effect, represent model/field uncertainty or replace independent LFMC validation. No independent-pixel p-values are calculated. When requirements fail, the CSV reports the reason and retains descriptive differences without inventing an interval. Each source map remains a separate observation. Same-date products are not silently averaged or mosaicked, and duplicate dates prevent interval estimation. docs.text: Available summarises the valid pixels independently on each date. It works with shifted native grids, including different Sentinel-3 overpasses. Cloud screening and changing coverage can alter which parts of a class contribute, so read the coverage panel alongside the LFMC curves. Common retains only pixel centres with valid predictions in every map. This is closest to the fixed-support summaries used in the paper's case studies. The maps must have identical grids and coordinates, and vegetation routing must agree on those common pixels. Shifted grids are rejected; no resampling is performed. A long or cloudy series can leave very few common pixels, or none. The table reports both available and retained counts. Summaries give equal weight to native pixel centres. They are not area-weighted statistics or fractions of pure vegetation cover. Grouping follows the maps' recorded model-routing categories and land-cover snapshot, rather than applying the GUI's land-cover selector to the saved maps again. docs.text: With vegetation groups enabled, the analysis also writes paired-date differences for Grass minus Shrub, Grass minus Tree and Shrub minus Tree. These differences are in LFMC percentage points . For example, class medians of 90% and 120% give a difference of −30 percentage points. Their temporal plot helps identify persistent contrasts and dates when those contrasts change. The shaded bands on the main figure describe spatial variability , not prediction confidence or statistical significance. Thousands of neighbouring pixels are not treated as independent replicates. For an optional exploratory temporal assessment, select Estimate exploratory paired-date vegetation contrast intervals . This selects common support and vegetation grouping. The calculation resamples blocks of consecutive paired dates, using a circular block bootstrap, and estimates an interval for the mean or median across those paired-date differences. The three intervals use a Bonferroni adjustment for a familywise confidence level of 95%. The method and end-to-start block construction are described in the bootstrap toolkit documentation . The package implements the small NumPy resampling calculation directly; that external toolkit is not a dependency. Intervals require unique, regularly spaced paired dates, common support and at least max(12, 4 × block length) paired observations. The default block length is three dates, with 2,000 resamples and recorded random seeds. These minimums are operational safeguards, not a guarantee of reliable inference. The method assumes that the paired-difference process is sufficiently stable over the selected period; that assumption is not automatically established. Seasonal trends, disturbances and long dependence can make it unsuitable. The comparison CSV reports interval limits and whether they exclude zero. This is exploratory evidence about model-derived temporal contrasts on the selected common pixels , conditional on the assumptions. It does not establish a causal vegetation effect, represent model/field uncertainty or replace independent LFMC validation. No independent-pixel p-values are calculated. When requirements fail, the CSV reports the reason and retains descriptive differences without inventing an interval. Each source map remains a separate observation. Same-date products are not silently averaged or mosaicked, and duplicate dates prevent interval estimation. docs.text: Troubleshooting Start with the failing command and its configuration. Preserve the provenance and relevant error text, but remove credentials and authentication tokens before sharing diagnostics. Python or GDAL fails on Windows Open a Conda-capable terminal and activate the environment before running Python, pip, tests or the CLI. A full path to python.exe does not by itself activate the environment's native-library paths. conda activate lfmc-multisensor python -c "import sys; print(sys.prefix)" python -m pip check Alternatively, use conda run --no-capture-output -n lfmc-multisensor before the Python command. Check that the prefix is the intended environment. If a native process fails, preserve the exit code and retry one small check before starting more jobs. Avoid running several large validation jobs while diagnosing an unstable environment. The explicit Windows lock includes the JPEG2000 driver needed by Sentinel-2. Installing an arbitrary rasterio/GDAL combination into an existing environment can leave that driver or its DLL dependencies unavailable. Credentials appear configured but downloading fails access-check reports configuration presence. Check the keys and expiry dates for CDSE (Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-3), the Earthdata account and token or login for MODIS/VIIRS, and your CDS token and AgERA5 terms for every workflow. docs.text: Make your first LFMC map This tutorial estimates live fuel moisture near Paradise, California, from the Sentinel-2 acquisition on 6 November 2018, two days before the Camp Fire. The small area lies within the extent shown in the paper's Appendix B . The tutorial uses WorldCover 2021 for vegetation routing and leaves weather downscaling off. The published Figure A3 uses a pre-fire Dynamic World composite and terrain-adjusted weather, so expect differences in coverage and LFMC. Complete the Conda installation and configure CDSE and CDS access first. The clone includes the three model bundles. Run every command below from the repository directory in the activated environment. To run the same configuration with file pickers, follow the desktop GUI tutorial . 1. Understand the request The file examples/sentinel2_camp_fire_2018.json contains these settings: { "bounds": [-121.66, 39.75, -121.62, 39.78], "day": "2018-11-06", "tile": "10TFK", "product_ids": ["4ffd9bb3-827b-4f8f-9cd1-bd81bdffe256"], "landcover_year": 2021, "landcover_policy": "fixed-year", "downscale": false, "models_dir": "../model-assets", "cache_dir": "../cache", "output": "../outputs/lfmc_camp_fire_20181106.tif" } bounds lists west, south, east and north in longitude/latitude degrees. The tile identifies the Sentinel-2 MGRS tile without its leading T . The date is the satellite acquisition and weather date. The selected 2021 WorldCover map determines which vegetation model is used at each output pixel. It is a fixed snapshot: you may keep 2021 or select 2020 for another acquisition year. To process a time series, add an inclusive end_day ; the configuration guide explains scene selection and dated outputs. Downscaling is initially disabled. Paths start from the directory containing the JSON file. Here, ../cache means the repository's cache directory, not a directory relative to your shell. Inspect the acquisition plan: lfmc-multisensor plan examples/sentinel2_camp_fire_2018.json This command does not contact providers. It lists the required inputs, including rainfall history back to 84 days before the analysis date. You do not need to download that history yourself. 2. Check access and select the scene lfmc-multisensor access-check examples/sentinel2_camp_fire_2018.json lfmc-multisensor discover examples/sentinel2_camp_fire_2018.json The access check reports configuration presence without showing secrets. The catalogue query checks the pinned CDSE product for this date, tile and area. When adapting the example to another area or date, remove the pinned product_ids and run discovery again. If several scenes match, set product_ids to the catalogue ID of the scene you want to run. Optional model preflight, in Python within the same Conda environment: from pathlib import Path from lfmc_multisensor.models import load_published_bundle for vegetation in ("Grass", "Shrub", "Tree"): path = Path("model-assets") / f"best_{vegetation}_gapfill_within_site.joblib" load_published_bundle(path, vegetation) print(vegetation, "model identity and contents checked") This extracts the bundles on first use and checks their hashes and contents before a large download. Use only the trusted model bundles from the repository. 3. Download inputs and predict lfmc-multisensor run examples/sentinel2_camp_fire_2018.json The workflow acquires the required satellite assets, prepares reflectance and quality masks, obtains terrain and land cover, and builds the weather predictors. It then selects the grass, shrub or tree model for eligible pixels and writes the results. Sentinel-2 with CDSE S3 keys fetches the required AOI windows. The first run also builds the weather cache, which can take longer than prediction while requests wait in the CDS queue. Keep the cache. If a download fails, rerun the same command with the same cache folder. Verified inputs are reused and incomplete downloads restart at the asset level. If the earlier attempt created output files, give the retry a new output name. For interrupted date ranges, see Cancel and recover . 4. Inspect the map and quality codes The example writes the following files. The names retain the source scene, processing baseline N0500 and LFMC model version v01 . outputs/ lfmc_camp_fire_20181106_S2B_MSIL2A_20181106T185559_N0500_R113_T10TFK_20230709T125120_LFMC_v01.tif lfmc_camp_fire_20181106_S2B_MSIL2A_20181106T185559_N0500_R113_T10TFK_20230709T125120_LFMC_v01_qa.tif lfmc_camp_fire_20181106_S2B_MSIL2A_20181106T185559_N0500_R113_T10TFK_20230709T125120_LFMC_v01_vegetation.tif lfmc_camp_fire_20181106_S2B_MSIL2A_20181106T185559_N0500_R113_T10TFK_20230709T125120_LFMC_v01.json The first GeoTIFF contains LFMC as percent dry mass. The QA raster explains where predictions are valid or missing. The JSON file records source identities, processing choices, model hashes and output hashes. Read these together when interpreting or sharing a map. Keep the vegetation companion with the other files to calculate AOI and vegetation time-series summaries without the original input cache. You can enable those summaries before mapping or analyse saved outputs later. from pathlib import Path import json import numpy as np import rasterio output = Path("outputs") / ( "lfmc_camp_fire_20181106_" "S2B_MSIL2A_20181106T185559_N0500_R113_T10TFK_20230709T125120_LFMC_v01.tif" ) with rasterio.open(output) as source: lfmc = source.read(1, masked=True) print("Grid:", source.crs, source.res, source.shape) with rasterio.open(output.with_name(output.stem + "_qa.tif")) as source: qa = source.read(1) valid = (qa == 0) & ~np.ma.getmaskarray(lfmc) print("Valid predictions:", int(valid.sum())) if valid.any(): print("Median LFMC (% dry mass):", float(np.median(lfmc.data[valid]))) provenance = json.loads(output.with_suffix(".json").read_text()) print("Vegetation counts:", provenance["classes"]) print("Weather mode:", provenance["weather_mode"]) The verified run produced 27,792 valid estimates out of 29,750 pixels (93.4%) on the 20 m grid. All pixels passed the optical screening. The remaining 1,958 had no eligible vegetation model, as shown by code 1 in the QA raster . 5. Try the optional weather adjustment The appendix methodology adjusts weather using local terrain elevation and a coarse reference elevation. The available reference is reconstructed from a fixed historical weather-model field; its equivalence to the provider's exact terrain and requested cycle has not been established. Keep original and adjusted results as distinct runs. Create a second configuration with a new output path: import json from pathlib import Path source = Path("examples/sentinel2_camp_fire_2018.json") configuration = json.loads(source.read_text()) configuration["downscale"] = True configuration["output"] = "../outputs/lfmc_camp_fire_20181106_downscaled.tif" Path("examples/sentinel2_camp_fire_2018_downscaled.json").write_text( json.dumps(configuration, indent=2) + "\n" ) lfmc-multisensor run examples/sentinel2_camp_fire_2018_downscaled.json This run automatically obtains the optional reference and reuses applicable cached inputs. The unadjusted run does not require that reference. A finer output grid or a changed prediction does not itself establish that the adjusted result is more accurate. 6. Move to another satellite The repository includes landsat8_2021.json , landsat9_2021.json , modis_2021.json , modis_aqua_2021.json , viirs_2021.json , sentinel3a_2021.json and sentinel3b_2021.json in examples/ . Their dates and sensor identifiers are deliberate. NASA products require Earthdata access; Sentinel-3 requires CDSE S3 keys and a .nc output path. For MODIS and VIIRS, retain composite_policy: contains-analysis-date and read the selected interval in the plan. The weather date does not turn an eight-day composite into a same-day satellite observation. For Sentinel-3, read the two-dimensional latitude/longitude coordinates in the NetCDF output. Use configuration and outputs before changing the area, date, product or file format.

docs.title: 2. Check access and select the scene

docs.text: lfmc-multisensor run examples/sentinel2_camp_fire_2018.json The workflow acquires the required satellite assets, prepares reflectance and quality masks, obtains terrain and land cover, and builds the weather predictors. It then selects the grass, shrub or tree model for eligible pixels and writes the results. Sentinel-2 with CDSE S3 keys fetches the required AOI windows. The first run also builds the weather cache, which can take longer than prediction while requests wait in the CDS queue. Keep the cache. If a download fails, rerun the same command with the same cache folder. Verified inputs are reused and incomplete downloads restart at the asset level. If the earlier attempt created output files, give the retry a new output name. For interrupted date ranges, see Cancel and recover .
docs.title: 3. Download inputs and predict

docs.text: The example writes the following files. The names retain the source scene, processing baseline N0500 and LFMC model version v01 . outputs/ lfmc_camp_fire_20181106_S2B_MSIL2A_20181106T185559_N0500_R113_T10TFK_20230709T125120_LFMC_v01.tif lfmc_camp_fire_20181106_S2B_MSIL2A_20181106T185559_N0500_R113_T10TFK_20230709T125120_LFMC_v01_qa.tif lfmc_camp_fire_20181106_S2B_MSIL2A_20181106T185559_N0500_R113_T10TFK_20230709T125120_LFMC_v01_vegetation.tif lfmc_camp_fire_20181106_S2B_MSIL2A_20181106T185559_N0500_R113_T10TFK_20230709T125120_LFMC_v01.json The first GeoTIFF contains LFMC as percent dry mass. The QA raster explains where predictions are valid or missing. The JSON file records source identities, processing choices, model hashes and output hashes. Read these together when interpreting or sharing a map. Keep the vegetation companion with the other files to calculate AOI and vegetation time-series summaries without the original input cache. You can enable those summaries before mapping or analyse saved outputs later. from pathlib import Path import json import numpy as np import rasterio output = Path("outputs") / ( "lfmc_camp_fire_20181106_" "S2B_MSIL2A_20181106T185559_N0500_R113_T10TFK_20230709T125120_LFMC_v01.tif" ) with rasterio.open(output) as source: lfmc = source.read(1, masked=True) print("Grid:", source.crs, source.res, source.shape) with rasterio.open(output.with_name(output.stem + "_qa.tif")) as source: qa = source.read(1) valid = (qa == 0) & ~np.ma.getmaskarray(lfmc) print("Valid predictions:", int(valid.sum())) if valid.any(): print("Median LFMC (% dry mass):", float(np.median(lfmc.data[valid]))) provenance = json.loads(output.with_suffix(".json").read_text()) print("Vegetation counts:", provenance["classes"]) print("Weather mode:", provenance["weather_mode"]) The verified run produced 27,792 valid estimates out of 29,750 pixels (93.4%) on the 20 m grid. All pixels passed the optical screening. The remaining 1,958 had no eligible vegetation model, as shown by code 1 in the QA raster .
docs.title: 4. Inspect the map and quality codes

docs.text: The appendix methodology adjusts weather using local terrain elevation and a coarse reference elevation. The available reference is reconstructed from a fixed historical weather-model field; its equivalence to the provider's exact terrain and requested cycle has not been established. Keep original and adjusted results as distinct runs. Create a second configuration with a new output path: import json from pathlib import Path source = Path("examples/sentinel2_camp_fire_2018.json") configuration = json.loads(source.read_text()) configuration["downscale"] = True configuration["output"] = "../outputs/lfmc_camp_fire_20181106_downscaled.tif" Path("examples/sentinel2_camp_fire_2018_downscaled.json").write_text( json.dumps(configuration, indent=2) + "\n" ) lfmc-multisensor run examples/sentinel2_camp_fire_2018_downscaled.json This run automatically obtains the optional reference and reuses applicable cached inputs. The unadjusted run does not require that reference. A finer output grid or a changed prediction does not itself establish that the adjusted result is more accurate.
docs.title: 5. Try the optional weather adjustment

docs.text: The repository includes landsat8_2021.json , landsat9_2021.json , modis_2021.json , modis_aqua_2021.json , viirs_2021.json , sentinel3a_2021.json and sentinel3b_2021.json in examples/ . Their dates and sensor identifiers are deliberate. NASA products require Earthdata access; Sentinel-3 requires CDSE S3 keys and a .nc output path. For MODIS and VIIRS, retain composite_policy: contains-analysis-date and read the selected interval in the plan. The weather date does not turn an eight-day composite into a same-day satellite observation. For Sentinel-3, read the two-dimensional latitude/longitude coordinates in the NetCDF output. Use configuration and outputs before changing the area, date, product or file format.
